notes: The popup now has a switch for automatic cleaning. Turning it off asks for how long: for 1 hour, until the browser restarts, or until you turn it back on. The popup says when cleaning comes back, and the toolbar icon stays grey until then. Alt+Shift+D also turns automatic cleaning off and on; you can change the key on your browser's extension shortcuts page (not on Firefox for Android, which has no keyboard shortcuts).
Firefox for Android: the Private list is now erased when the last private tab closes even if you opened the extension from a private tab. In 1.3.0 that kept the list until the next browser start.

Firefox for Android is now supported, including Fennec and other browsers that install add-ons from addons.mozilla.org. Firefox for Android's own "Delete browsing data on quit" has no per-site exceptions, so the Keep list fills that gap: kept sites keep their cookies and everything else is cleared. Turn off Firefox's own delete-on-quit for cookies, or it removes kept sites too. Containers and context menus don't exist on Android, so those settings are hidden there, and container lists in a backup from desktop Firefox are merged into the Default list, as on Chrome. Sites kept from private tabs are forgotten when the last private tab closes, or at the next browser start.

Keep rules that keep only some cookies can now use patterns for cookie names: "auth_*" keeps every cookie whose name starts with "auth_" ("\*" is a real asterisk). Type a name or pattern in the box above a rule's cookie list; each pattern shows which of the site's cookies it covers.

Heads-up for exports: older versions of this extension and Cookie AutoDelete read "auth_*" as one literal cookie name, so a rule with patterns imported there cleans those cookies instead of keeping them. Rules already saved keep working as before: on update, any "*" in a saved cookie name is escaped so it still means that one cookie. Only importing an older export that names a cookie with a real "*" reads it as a pattern; write "\*" for a literal asterisk.

Firefox: the settings page and Help now say that Firefox can't delete a site's cache, Cache Storage or file-system storage automatically, and how to clear them yourself in the meantime (or try Brave, where the extension does).
The Overview and Help pages now explain how to pin the extension in your own browser: Chrome's puzzle icon, Firefox's Extensions button, or Firefox for Android's menu.
Updates are quieter: the settings page now opens by itself only after a new major version. Release notes for every version stay here on the Overview page.
Internal: the Firefox test matrix records a full Firefox for Android pass, and the store permission notes describe how site data is cleared on Chromium browsers.

Firefox: a keep rule in one container no longer keeps a site's Local Storage and IndexedDB from being cleaned outside that container. For example, if you keep YouTube in a container, the data of YouTube videos embedded on other sites is now cleaned when those sites close, and the container keeps its own YouTube data. A site's service worker data still stays everywhere while any container keeps the site, because Firefox can only clear it in all containers at once.
Internal: the automated Firefox suite checks a video player kept in a container, and the Firefox test matrix records the test pass for 1.2.2.

Firefox: the storage that frames from other sites keep inside a page (for example an embedded YouTube player's Local Storage) is now cleaned once the embedding site closes. Before, it stayed unless the frame's site had a cookie of its own. It is left alone while the frame's own site is open in a tab, still embedded in another open site, or kept by one of your rules, because Firefox clears stored data host by host and would clear that site's own data too. For this, the extension now also notes the address of frames from other sites as they load, as it already did for same-site frames; it never sees their content.

A keep rule for a site no longer keeps that site's cookies stored under other sites you don't keep (Total Cookie Protection on Firefox, CHIPS on Chrome). For example, a rule for youtube.com keeps your YouTube sign-in, but no longer keeps the cookies of a YouTube video embedded on a site you don't keep. To keep an embed such as Disqus comments signed in on a site, keep that site too. The cookie list in the rule editor now shows only the cookies a rule can keep.

The Overview page now shows the extension's name. After an update to a new major or minor version, the settings page opens with a notice and a "See what's new" button that jumps to these release notes. Patch updates no longer open the settings page.

Internal: the automated Firefox suite now runs from macOS 27 app terminals and checks the storage of cross-site frames and the keep rules for partitioned cookies, the Firefox test matrix records the embedded-frame CI results, and the store listings have a new before/after promo image.

Chrome, Edge and Brave: sites no longer stay listed in Edge's "All cookies and site data" after a cleanup. Edge keeps a small record for each part of a site that is not a regular cookie, and the extension could not reach it; it is now cleared once a site has no cookies left. A site you keep cookies for keeps that record too, because clearing it would also delete the kept cookies.

Chrome, Edge and Brave: cookies that secure (https) pages set without the Secure flag are now deleted when the browser ties each cookie to the kind of address that set it. Before, such cookies, the extension's own hidden marker cookie included, could stay behind.
When a site sets cookies again right after its cleanup, for example from requests still finishing when its tab closed, the extension now cleans again instead of leaving them until your next visit.
A keep rule for a site no longer keeps the third-party cookies stored under it (Total Cookie Protection on Firefox, CHIPS on Chrome). Those cookies are kept only by a rule for their own site.
Chrome, Edge and Brave: the Cleanup log, the cleaned-cookie counter and the notification now count only cookies that were really deleted.

Internal: the automated Chrome suite now also checks cookies tied to secure addresses, kept cookies that share a name with deleted ones, and the removal counts. The Firefox store screenshots no longer fail on a window-sizing race, and the build and test tools were updated.

Firefox: the Protection page has a new Firefox containers card, where each container can be given its own keep list. It is off by default, and until you turn it on the Default list covers every container.
Firefox: keeping a site from the right-click menu in a container tab now saves the rule to the list that actually applies to that tab.
Firefox: Saved sites can copy the Default list's rules into a container's own list, so switching separate lists on does not leave a container with an empty keep list.

Keep rules made in private windows are now erased when the last private window closes, so your settings keep no record of sites you visited privately. When Firefox is set to never remember history, every window is private and these rules stay saved. Rules already in the Private list are erased after updating, the first time a normal window is open with no private window.
Copying the Default list into a container and importing a saved-sites file now land in one step instead of one rule at a time, so long lists no longer stall the Saved sites page.
Firefox ESR 140: the popup's cookie count and "Delete this site's cookies" now include third-party cookies stored under sites on a non-standard port, such as local development servers.
Firefox: version 140 or newer is now required. Firefox 128 ESR stopped getting updates in August 2025; anyone still on it keeps the previous version of the extension.

The Public Suffix List used to tell sites apart was updated: sites on more hosting platforms (for example surge.sh, Heroku's newer app addresses, cloud.run and ai.studio) are now cleaned separately, and several discontinued or test-only platforms are no longer split per site.
Every non-English language now has its own wording for the Saved sites list selector, the Firefox containers card and the site-access banner, which had been showing English.
The Support page now fills in your browser version and operating system in the details you copy for a bug report.
You can report a bug without a GitHub account: the Support page's "Email a bug report" button opens your mail app with the details already filled in.

Site data is now cleaned from every part of a site, not just its main address: what the site's other pages and its frames on subdomains stored (for example a sign-in or device-check frame) is deleted with it. For this the extension now asks for the webRequest permission, which lets it see the address of each page and frame as it loads; it never sees their content and never blocks or changes anything.

Keep rules now also decide whether a subdomain's stored data stays. To keep everything a site stores, use a rule that covers its subdomains (*.example.com), which is what the popup's "Keep cookies for this site" button adds.
Chrome, Edge and Brave: Cache Storage is now deleted together with service workers, and file-system storage together with IndexedDB, so "Delete all site data" no longer leaves them behind.
Chrome, Edge and Brave: in incognito windows the extension no longer puts its hidden marker cookie into your normal cookies, where it kept a record of the site you visited privately.
Chrome, Edge and Brave: in incognito windows the popup's cookie count, the toolbar badge and "Delete this site's cookies" now use the incognito window's cookies instead of your normal ones.
Chrome, Edge and Brave: keeping a site from an incognito window now saves the rule to the Private list, so it is erased with the private session instead of staying in your Default list.
The Advanced section under "Delete all site data" and the entries of the Cleanup log open again when your system's animations are turned off (for example Windows' Animation effects setting).

Internal: the local check run before a pull request now runs exactly what CI runs, code scanning is back on, and the Bun and Node versions are pinned in one place. The automated Firefox suite no longer fails on a flaky driver download, runs on both the ESR and the current release, and covers nearly every row of the manual test matrix. A new automated suite drives Chrome and checks what site-data cleanup leaves in storage.
The Support page now has separate links for reporting bugs and for questions and discussions.
The Support page now links to the official Firefox Add-ons listing.
The debug panel now shows Firefox-specific details when debug mode is enabled.
Internal: the build pipeline was hardened (CI actions pinned to audited revisions) and the automated Firefox test suite was stabilized.
Toolbar icon updates are now debounced per tab instead of globally, so the icon stays accurate when many tabs change at once.
Internal: every release is now checked by an automated end-to-end suite driving the packaged extension in a real Firefox.
Firefox is now supported, including containers, Total Cookie Protection, and First-Party Isolation.
The popup and expression lists are container-aware on Firefox.
Site domains are now determined with the real Public Suffix List for more accurate cleaning.
Partitioned cookies are handled on both browsers (Total Cookie Protection on Firefox, CHIPS on Chrome).
Turning on automatic cleaning no longer wipes existing site data unless you explicitly opt in and confirm.
Sites protected by an open tab or a keep rule are guarded across all cookie stores.
The Share menu and homepage link now point to the Chrome Web Store listing.
The Overview page now shows how to turn on automatic cleaning and pin the toolbar icon.
Keeping or unkeeping a site now updates the toolbar icon in every open tab, not just the active one.
Initial release of Auto-Delete Cookies for Privacy.
